name: core.openwop.workflows.assistant
description: WF-COS-1 — the ADR 0023 assistant's six boot-path workflows, migrated off the in-tree `registerWorkflow({...})` pin sites in `features/assistant/loops.ts` and `features/assistant/actionExecution.ts`. THREE PERCEPTION LOOPS (calendar ingest, drive ingest, morning briefing) fired by the RFC 0052 scheduler, and THREE APPROVED-ACTION EXECUTIONS (email send, calendar invite, calendar reschedule) dispatched by the winning approval claim. Each is registered chain-backed under its ORIGINAL workflowId, so the per-tenant scheduler job rows, the `EXEC_WORKFLOW_BY_KIND` dispatch and every existing run stamp keep resolving — and all six become gallery-visible and builder-editable like every other chain. NO credential or connection material lives in any node config: the ADR 0024 §4 Option-C opt-in is RUN-LEVEL (`configurable.connections`), set on the scheduler job / at dispatch, exactly as it was before the migration.

chains.label: Assistant — calendar ingestion loop
chains.description: Reads upcoming Google Calendar events through the Connections broker and maintains prep commitments in the memory graph (idempotent; sources stamped untrusted). The fetch node carries NO connection annotation — the host injects the enabling principal's write-scoped token when the URL matches Google's curated apiHosts, per the run-level opt-in on the scheduler job.

chains.label: Assistant — drive ingestion loop
chains.description: Reads recently-modified Google Drive files through the Connections broker and maintains review commitments in the memory graph (idempotent; sources stamped untrusted).

chains.label: Assistant — morning briefing
chains.description: Composes a source-grounded brief (top commitments with citations, what is at risk, today's meetings, what awaits approval) and drops it in the Notifications inbox. A single graph-read node with `notify:true`; no external I/O at all. The node is `role:"side-effect"` (WF-COS-2), so a `:fork` is served the recorded outcome rather than re-briefing.

chains.label: Assistant — send an approved email
chains.description: Executes an approved `email.send` action. `prepare-action-request` is a pure transform of the run's `action` input into a Gmail base64url raw message; the fetch performs the send AS the approving human (the run's `metadata.actingUserId`), so the ADR 0024 Phase-D resolver picks THEIR write-scoped connection and fails closed when write re-consent was never granted; `confirm-action-send` is the verdict gate — an HTTP fetch completes on ANY outcome, so without it a refused send would record as `sent`.

chains.label: Assistant — send an approved calendar invite
chains.description: Executes an approved `calendar.invite` action. Same three-node shape as the email send, including the `confirm-action-send` verdict gate.

chains.label: Assistant — apply an approved reschedule
chains.description: Executes an approved `calendar.reschedule` action. The URL carries the `{{eventId}}` placeholder the prepare node's output substitutes, and the verb is PATCH; otherwise identical to the invite chain.
